note: Two documents in one, and they are cited separately. The HABS architectural description (1963) is this record. Pages 7-21 also transcribe John J. Glessner's March 1923 booklet The Story of a House, which is period testimony by the owner and is cited as glessner_story_of_a_house_1923 so that its date is carried with it. THE ALTERATIONS PARAGRAPH IS WHAT MAKES THE DRAWINGS USABLE FOR 1904: it lists what the September 1946 research-centre conversion changed (stable loft and basement partitioned, stable door replaced, loft door closed up, stable/kitchen/laundry fixtures and the coal furnace removed, school-room woodwork painted, the door of the underpass on the east facade replaced, the courtyard entirely paved as a parking lot) and says the original plan, finishes and permanent furniture were left untouched. It names no change to the masonry envelope or the roofs. The legal description on p. 1: Block 9, lots 38, 39 and 40 of the Assessor's Division of the SW fractional 1/4 of Section 22, T39N, R14E; Glessner bought lots 39, 40 and the north 17 feet of lot 38 on March 24, 1885 (Book 502A pp. 77-79; Document 616860). Note the wall-material name: 'Wellesley Granite' (p. 21), which is also Glessner's 1923 word; the house museum's own page says Braggville pink granite (recorded in the Prairie library's dossier as G02). The disagreement is carried, not resolved.
what_it_supplies: the exterior construction as surveyed in 1963: foundations of Joliet limestone ending at the ground line; brick walls faced with alternately six- and eight-inch sheets of granite with deeper returns at openings; courtyard walls of light pink brick with Joliet limestone lintels and sills; steeply pitched gabled roofs covered with tar-covered terracotta tiles six inches wide, five inches exposed; copper sheathing on the roof of the entrance-hall bow
the original east carriage (porte-cochere) door as seen in a 1945 photograph: two heavily panelled leaves with heavy iron straps and latches
the list of 1946 alterations, which is the phase filter every 1963 dimension has to pass for 1904
the legal description and the March 1885 purchase of lots 39, 40 and the north 17 ft of lot 38
what_it_does_not_supply: the widths of lots 38-40 in feet: the lot sizes of the Assessor's Division block are not stated
the date the stable became a garage, the date the roof tiles were tarred, or any other change between 1887 and 1946 that it does not list
measurements: the data pages describe; the drawings (habs_glessner_house_il_1015_drawings) measure
